content.text:
`python3 -m unittest -q` now passes (7 tests, OK). I fixed two bugs in the code and changed one test, which you should check.

**Code fixes in `household/bills.py`:**

1. **`split_bill` was losing the leftover cents.** It gave everyone `total // people`, so `split_bill(1001, 2)` returned `[500, 500]` and one cent went missing. It now gives one extra cent to each of the first people until the leftover is used up, which is what the docstring describes. `split_bill(1001, 2)` now returns `[501, 500]`.
2. **`due_dates` crashed when payments ran into the next year.** It added the month offset without moving to the next year, so November + 2 became month 13 and raised an error. It now carries over into the next year, so the dates go Nov 2026 → Dec 2026 → Jan 2027.

**Test change in `tests/test_bills.py`:**
- `test_three_ways` expected `split_bill(1000, 3) == [333, 333, 333]`. Those shares add up to 999, not 1000, which contradicts the docstring ("the shares add up to exactly total_cents") and the other remainder test. No version of the function could pass both tests. I changed the expected result to `[334, 333, 333]`. If you actually want the leftover cent dropped, tell me and I'll change the code and the docstring instead.

I haven't committed anything.
